title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1972-09-16
lineage: 7" SBDMR > Cass > DAT > CDn > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy September ’72 show with a smoking Dark Star → Brokedown Palace sequence captured on solid soundboard tape
ai_review.review: The performance is driven by an epic, 26‑minute Dark Star that bursts into a ferocious “Tiger” jam before dissolving into a heartfelt Brokedown Palace, with Jerry’s wah‑wah guitar and Keith’s dazzling keys taking center stage. The soundboard source is clear enough for the jams to shine, though vocals sit a bit forward, making it a solid but not flawless listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Eight detailed reviews average 4.38 stars; the show is praised for its standout Dark Star and overall energy, while recording quality is consistently described as good with only minor vocal balance issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear soundboard capture; vocals are a little loud compared to the mix, but overall clarity and instrument separation are solid for the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a smoking Playin', moves through Morning Dew and Greatest, then launches into an expansive Dark Star that transitions seamlessly into a soaring Brokedown Palace, keeping momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Smokey wah‑wah guitar work; described as “all over the show” with killer leads in the Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Took the night off and sounded dull, a noticeable dip in bass presence for this date.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith delivers fantastic, ferocious keys during the post‑verse ‘Tiger’ jam.
